definitions.gloss: to pierce; to stick into; to become embedded in
definitions.explanation: For a sharp object to penetrate and become lodged in something. An intransitive verb describing the result of piercing — the object is stuck in place.

definitions.gloss: to pierce emotionally; to cut deep; to hit home
definitions.explanation: For words, a gaze, or a feeling to affect someone deeply and sharply, as if piercing them. A figurative extension of the physical meaning.

examples.japanese: とげが{指|ゆび}に{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さった。
examples.english: A thorn stuck into my finger.

examples.japanese: ガラスの{破片|はへん}が{足|あし}に{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さった。
examples.english: A shard of glass pierced my foot.

examples.japanese: {矢|や}が{的|まと}の{真|ま}ん{中|なか}に{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さっていた。
examples.english: An arrow was stuck right in the center of the target.

examples.japanese: {鋭|するど}い{視線|しせん}が{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さる。
examples.english: A sharp gaze pierces through me.

examples.japanese: その{言葉|ことば}が{胸|むね}に{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さった。
{冷|つめ}たい{風|かぜ}が{肌|はだ}に{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さるように{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: The cold wind stings painfully as if piercing the skin.

notes:
A compound verb from {突|つ}く (to poke, to thrust) + {刺|さ}さる (to stick in). The intransitive partner of {突|つ}き{刺|さ}す (to stab into — transitive). Emphasizes the result: the sharp object is lodged in place.

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive. The transitive counterpart is {突|つ}き{刺|さ}す.
- {突|つ}き{刺|さ}さる — the thorn stuck in (intransitive, focus on result)
- {突|つ}き{刺|さ}す — to stab something (transitive, focus on action)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- とげが{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さる — a thorn sticks in
- {視線|しせん}が{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さる — a gaze pierces
- {胸|むね}に{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さる — to pierce one's heart
- {言葉|ことば}が{突|つ}き{刺|さ}さる — words pierce/cut deep

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {刺|さ}さる — to stick in, to prick (simpler; without the forceful thrust nuance)
- {貫|つらぬ}く — to penetrate, to pierce through (goes all the way through, not lodged)
- {突|つ}き{刺|さ}す — to stab into (transitive counterpart)
